items.summary: The Empirical-Axiomatic Framework (EAF) is a broader foundational framework concerned with existence, ontological structure, consistency, logic, information, representation, knowledge, scientific modelling, consciousness, and related philosophical questions. This paper develops the epistemological part of EAF by establishing a conceptual relation between underlying structures, representations, information, self, epistemic architecture, epistemic capacity, and knowledge. The paper distinguishes the Universal Information Space from the Ontological Information Space and defines knowledge as information possessed by a self, where a self is understood as a well-defined system. It further distinguishes generalised knowledge from Traditional Knowledge, with Traditional Knowledge requiring comprehended structural correspondence between a representation and the underlying structure it represents. The paper analyses epistemic activities, knowledge generation, representation changes, generator bases, and the limitations of epistemic systems. It distinguishes incomplete representations from incorrect representations and epistemic limitations from ontological limitations. A computer is examined as a detailed example of a non-biological epistemic system capable of acquiring, storing, processing, transforming, representing, and communicating information without these capacities necessarily implying consciousness or Traditional Knowledge. The framework is then applied to major epistemological and related philosophical problems, including induction, Gödel’s incompleteness problem, material implication, the philosophy of mathematics, Benacerraf’s problem, Gettier’s problem, demarcation, the Münchhausen trilemma, Sorites, and universals. The paper does not claim to provide final solutions to all these problems. Rather, it offers a unified conceptual basis for reframing them through the relations among existence, structure, representation, information, and epistemic systems. The resulting framework provides a foundation for further formal, scientific, and philosophical development within EAF.

items.summary: What two millennia of transmitting a canon with no living author, no writing and an active schism left behind — seven copy-integrity mechanisms with engineering forms, offered to any retrieval system that must hand a machine reader something checkable; and the finding that what the transmission left was divergence made detectable, never divergence prevented. A retrieval system that serves text to a machine reader has a problem the machine reader cannot solve for itself: the reader cannot tell a faithful copy from a plausible one. Provenance-Carrying Retrieval argued that the response should therefore carry the means of its own falsification — a hash, an independent time anchor, a citable identifier — and that the trust burden should be inverted, so that a server ships the tools to disbelieve it. This paper asks a different and prior question. Has anything ever actually run this problem to completion? One thing has, and it is not a computer system. The Theravāda Pāli canon was transmitted for roughly four centuries with no written copy at all, and for roughly two millennia in total, without a living author to arbitrate, across schism — on the Sri Lankan chronicles' account, one that produced a rival recital — through famine, war, and the ordinary attrition of the human beings who were the storage medium. That is a copy-integrity problem under a threat model that overlaps a retrieval server's without being the same one (§7 partitions the two), sustained for a duration no production system has approached. It converged on an apparatus, and this paper reads seven of its parts as engineering. All seven are transpositions, and the paper says so plainly. Five transpose practices the archival and transparency-log communities already know under other names: an inline attribution formula opening the text rather than a metadata field (§4.1); admission decided at build time by a named assembly under a recorded procedure rather than by a query-time filter (§4.2); commentary labelled as a distinct text class , from which a server inherits an obligation never to substitute generated summary for source (§4.3); variant readings preserved with their line of transmission attached rather than normalised to a preferred text (§4.4); and abridgement announced inline at the point of the cut (§4.5). Two more transpose practices known in other fields: interpretive standing carried per passage rather than per document, because an excerpt loses its document's front matter at retrieval (§4.6); and scheduled public re-verification before an assembly in which silence is a positive assertion for which the silent party is accountable (§4.7). An eighth item is a convention rather than a mechanism — every exclusion served with the case that occasioned it (§4.8). Two further designs (§5) are carried furthest from where the destination field keeps them. The conformance endpoint (§5.1) accepts a claimed quotation and returns a disposition on the claim , together with the procedure to follow next, and by construction returns no disposition on the claimant — the part a hash does not have, because a hash reports that a comparison failed and says nothing about what to do. It is offered as a new composition: closed disposition sets about a submitted object are old (OCSP), and what is new is a set over a multi-recension corpus that includes a conforming variant with its witness. The separated completeness manifest (§5.2) is a signed, versioned and expiring statement of a collection's membership and cardinality published as an artifact distinct from the index it describes, on the ground that an index cannot attest to its own completeness : a silently dropped document is invisible to every check that reads the index, and detectable to a third party holding only the manifest. items.summary: This chapter explores the epistemic tensions faced by researchers, particularly those from formerly colonized countries in the Global South, caught between the demands of scientific neutrality and ethical engagement with the coloniality of knowledge. items.summary: Optimal control theory delivers magnetic-field pulses that reverse a magnetic moment for the least dissipated energy, and recent work shows these pulses reach picosecond, energy-efficient switching in two-dimensional van der Waals magnets. Because the optimal pulse is always perpendicular to the moment, it exerts no restoring torque on the transverse perturbations that thermal fluctuations excite, so the switching becomes unreliable exactly where it matters. A longitudinal field parallel to the moment removes that instability and is invisible to the leading-order dynamics, so it is often described as a cost-free stabilizer. It is not free: it adds the square of its amplitude integrated over the pulse to the switching cost. This preprint computes, for the first time, the cost-reliability front of that longitudinal field. Using an open-source engine (spinoct) that solves optimal control over the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, and a stochastic thermostat validated against the Boltzmann distribution, we reproduce the published stabilization physics for monolayer CrSBr, the half-hyperbolic bare reversal path and the counterintuitive success-rate dip near a half anisotropy field, and we add the missing axis: the added switching cost, which grows quadratically with the longitudinal field and reaches about 1.5e-10 T^2 s at 2.5 anisotropy fields for a demanding thermal-stability factor of twenty. The front makes the reliability-versus-energy trade explicit and quantitative, and lets a device designer read off the smallest field that reaches a target reliability. The switching cost is reported in its model-free units of tesla-squared-seconds, never converted to joules without an explicit circuit model. All quantitative results are reproduced from artifacts committed to the repository, and a live instance is open. Engine (MIT): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_SpinOCT . Product and live instance (MIT): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RES_Espira ; https://espira.fasl-work.com .

items.summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.

items.summary: English — Abstract U = Δ develops an operational-relational framework that takes difference, rather than objects, substances, space, time, or motion, as the minimal condition from which a finite description of a physical world can be constructed. The starting expression U=ΔU=\Delta is progressively developed through a finite observational window W=(σW,τW)W=(\sigma_W,\tau_W) , which determines the spatial and temporal resolution at which differences can be distinguished. Differences below that resolution are compressed, while the resolved field is represented through successive saturations. Within each saturation, relatively stable regions are treated as conventions rather than absolute entities. Every convention is defined together with its complement and acquires an operational boundary. Persistence is then reconstructed not as immobility or intrinsic identity, but as a history of reconfirmations across successive readings under the same window. Relative persistence, local spatiotemporal comparison, boundary redrawing, deformation, movement, emergence and disappearance are developed from this common relational structure. The dynamical part of the work studies evolution as a recursive process of local reattribution between successive saturations. A resolved convention can retain the same macroscopic extension while undergoing non-zero internal turnover; consequently, stability does not imply absence of process. Incoming and outgoing reattributions are treated as complementary descriptions of the same local transitions, while coherent patterns of reattribution can give rise to macroscopic notions such as motion and flow rather than requiring them as primitive variables. The remaining development investigates the minimal mathematical closure of this recursive evolution, the reconstruction of changing adjacency and boundary networks, the effect of changing observational windows and resolution scales, and the conditions under which the resulting framework can support quantitative prediction and empirical falsification. Particular attention is given to distinguishing logical consequences, operational definitions, scale-dependent descriptions, and constitutive or empirical laws that must be independently calibrated. The aim is therefore not to replace established physical theories with an assumed microscopic ontology, but to investigate a minimal grammar through which resolved objects, persistence, boundaries, dynamics and continuity may emerge from recursively organized difference. L’espressione iniziale U=ΔU=\Delta viene sviluppata attraverso una finestra osservativa finita W=(σW,τW)W=(\sigma_W,\tau_W) , che determina la risoluzione spaziale e temporale alla quale le differenze possono essere distinte. Le differenze sottosoglia vengono compresse, mentre il campo risolto viene rappresentato attraverso saturazioni successive. All’interno di ogni saturazione, le regioni relativamente stabili vengono trattate come convenzioni e non come entità assolute. Ogni convenzione è definita insieme al proprio complemento e acquisisce un bordo operativo. La persistenza viene quindi ricostruita non come immobilità o identità intrinseca, ma come storia di riconferme attraverso letture successive effettuate sotto la stessa finestra. Persistenza relazionale, confronto spazio-temporale locale, ridisegno dei bordi, deformazione, movimento, emergenza e scomparsa vengono sviluppati a partire dalla stessa struttura relazionale. items.summary: This record contains three components from the SLD experiment at the SLAC Linear Collider (SLC): the reconstructed mini-Data Summary Tapes (mini-DSTs) covering the full 1996–1998 data-taking periods, the corresponding simulated (Monte Carlo) mini-DSTs, and an AI-ready corpus of digitized SLD-era internal documentation. This version (v3) adds the simulated samples to the reconstructed data and documentation corpus released in v2, and supersedes the earlier releases. Both the collision events and the simulated events are made available in two formats: the native binary “jazelle” columnar format used by the SLD reconstruction software, and a derived Apache Parquet translation that is convenient for modern columnar analysis tools (PyArrow, pandas, awkward, polars, ...). The two formats contain identical physics content. The Parquet version is the one most users will want. Reconstructed data 68 mini-DST files covering the 1996, 1997, and 1998 runs. After translation and reading via the  jazelle  Python package, the dataset contains 658,241 reconstructed events. The center-of-mass energy is at the Z pole (√s ≈ 91.2 GeV) and the electron beam was longitudinally polarized, with mean magnitude 76.14% for the 1996 run and 73.08% for the 1997–1998 runs. Per-event polarization values are recorded in the PHBM bank. Bank families Reconstruction outputs are organized into “bank families”, each describing one detector subsystem or one stage of the reconstruction chain. The banks present in this release: IEVENTH  — event header (run/event ID, trigger mask, timestamp). PHBM  — beam information (beam energy, beam polarization magnitude and sign, interaction-point position and uncertainty). PHPSUM  — inclusive list of reconstructed physics particles (4-momentum, charge, origin coordinates). PHCHRG  — charged-track helix parameters, error matrices, hit counts, fit quality, and dE/dx from the Central Drift Chamber (CDC) and VXD3 vertex detector. PHKLUS  — calorimeter clusters from the Liquid Argon Calorimeter (LAC), with raw and per-layer energies. PHCRID  — Cherenkov ring likelihoods for particle identification from the Cherenkov Ring Imaging Detector (CRID). PHWIC  — muon tracking in the Warm Iron Calorimeter (WIC). PHKELID  — electron identification from track-calorimeter matching. PHPOINT  — master pointer bank linking each PHPSUM entry to its associated track (PHCHRG) and/or calorimeter cluster (PHKLUS), enabling per-particle access to detector-level quantities. PHKCHRG  — track-to-cluster matching kinematics. The mini-DSTs are the reduced-format event records produced by the SLD reconstruction. They contain enough information for typical physics analyses (event shapes, electroweak asymmetries, jet clustering) but not the full raw detector data. Only the standard reconstruction-level data-quality requirements suppressing non-collision backgrounds are applied. No channel-specific event selection is pre-applied. Further documentation on the jazelle file format and the field-level contents of each bank can be found in the README of the jazelle package GitHub repository (see “Related identifiers” for a link). items.summary: This repository contains the code and data used to prepare a manuscript titled "Flow dependence of boundary-layer scheme parameters revealed by stochastic inversion".  Code: The data were produced with two different ideal cases of the Weather Research and Forecasting Model (WRF): (1) WRFlux v1.7.0 in large-eddy simulation (LES) configuration, available at https://github.com/matzegoebel/WRFlux/ and (2) WRF v4.4.2 in single-column model configuration ( https://github.com/wrf-model/WRF/releases/tag/v4.4.2 ).  The LES and SCM simulations represent the evolution of a convective boundary layer in the atmosphere over flat terrain. To reproduce the LES simulation, download WRFlux v1.7.0 from the link above, compile as usual and run it using the namelist file and input sounding provided in LES.zip.  To reproduce the deterministic SCM simulations, a modified version of WRF v4.4.2 is needed. Download WRF v4.4.2 and replace the corresponding files with those provided in this repository under WRF_SCM.zip, then compile as usual. These modifications allow for variable parameters in the YSU planetary boundary layer (PBL) scheme instead of prescribed constant ones. The parameter values are controlled via the namelist: ysu_pfactor ( p ), ysu_bfactor ( b ), and ysu_entrainment_hfx_mag ( Ae ). WRF_SCM.zip also contains the namelist file, input sounding, and surface forcing file (scmflx_bdy) needed to run the simulation. The input sounding and scmflx_bdy files are the same for all SCM runs. To reproduce the ensemble of SCM simulations, the modified version of WRF coupled with a modified version of DART-WRF v2024.2.20 ( https://github.com/lkugler/DART-WRF/releases/tag/v2024.2.20 ) is needed. Here, DART-WRF is used only to generate an ensemble of forecasts. Download DART-WRF v2024.2.20 and copy the files provided in DART-WRF_SCM.zip into the matching paths of the DART-WRF source tree, overwriting the originals. DART-WRF_SCM.zip also contains the parameter perturbation files needed to run the large ensembles (as .txt files). The large ensembles are subject to parameter perturbations only. For further details on all simulations, please refer to the manuscript. Data: LES.zip: contains the WRFlux output (instout_d01_2001-06-05_07_00_00_compressed.nc) from which synthetic observations are drawn in this study. SCM_deterministic.zip: contains all deterministic SCM runs.  wrfout_d01_2001-06-05_07:00:00.nc: SCM output with original prescribed parameter values (see manuscript). SINGLE_PARAMETER_PERTURBATION_EXP: contains directories for each parameter with varying parameter values (still deterministic runs), e.g., in Ae_0.0 parameter Ae is set to 0 and the other two parameters remain at their prescribed values. SCM_ensemble.zip: contains all SCM ensemble runs produced with the modified version of WRF via DART-WRF. items.summary: This paper proves four independent conditions under which a system's perceived state can become detached from its true state, and shows what follows when that detachment coincides with self-reinforcing dynamics that make an eventual correction harder to reverse than it was to prevent. A sequence of individually imperceptible changes can accumulate to arbitrary cumulative drift without any single step ever being flagged. Two independent, fully rational reasons can lead a corrective judgment to be legitimately suspended: genuine uncertainty about the reliability of one's own instrument, and a collapse of verification incentive below a sharp cost threshold. Even a fully active, fully resourced, fully self-trusting corrector faces a hard information-theoretic ceiling on accuracy once the signal distinguishing genuine change from ordinary variation grows statistically indistinguishable. A population state governed by a bandwagon-reinforced dynamic exhibits a trichotomy of long-run outcomes separated by a hysteresis gap, so reversing an already-shifted state requires strictly more than what triggered the shift. Together, these results suggest a precise reading of familiar worries about smartphone habits, synthetic media, and self-reinforcing online communities, not as vague metaphors, but as specific, checkable conditions under which an unnoticed and hard-to-reverse drift becomes possible.

items.summary: This research edition studies a concrete finite part of the Riemann zeta function's spectral data. A packet is a chosen finite collection of its zeros, with every selected multiplicity retained. Its polynomial h divides the completed function g=2xi. The original theta-function source has Mellin transform g/h. Tensor products of this source represent sums of the selected zero jets, including their full repeated-root structure. The purpose is to calculate the cost of those spectral configurations in the original arithmetic source norm. It is not to choose a favorable new metric or to assert that an off-critical-line zero exists. What to read Main research reader, 482 pages. The complete literature-and-proof synthesis now includes Section 41 on arithmetic source/relation volumes and Section 42 on gamma convolution descent. The end of Section 42 proves the direct analytic generating-function map into the same Toda input. Split-Zero/Toda companion, 424 pages. items.summary: Abstract: Livestock production is central to rural livelihoods across sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in pastoral, agro-pastoral, and smallholder farming systems. Livestock provide food, income, savings, employment, insurance against shocks, manure, and social and cultural capital. However, the contribution of livestock to household welfare depends not only on production but also on households' ability to participate effectively in livestock markets and obtain fair returns. This review synthesizes literature published primarily between 2020 and 2026, with particular attention to pastoral and smallholder systems in East Africa. The evidence shows that market infrastructure, market information, producer organizations, transport, veterinary services, financial services, value addition, and improved market governance can reduce transaction costs, increase market participation, improve producer returns, and strengthen livelihood resilience. Evidence from Ethiopia demonstrates that improved livestock market sheds can increase smallholder earnings, while evidence from northern Kenya indicates that improvements in physical and communication infrastructure have strengthened market integration. However, market participation does not automatically improve welfare. Drought, climate variability, conflict, distress sales, weak bargaining power, gender inequalities, inadequate services, and restrictions on pastoral mobility can limit or reverse livelihood gains. Informal information networks, brokers, customary institutions, and cross-border trade also remain important in connecting remote producers to markets. The review therefore argues that livestock marketing should move beyond increasing sales volumes toward resilient, inclusive, equitable, and sustainable livestock value chains. Effective interventions should integrate market infrastructure, information, producer organization, animal health, finance, value addition, climate-risk management, gender empowerment, rangeland governance, conflict management, and predictable trade regulation.

items.summary: Voice is among the most studied non-invasive signals for Parkinson's disease detection, with reported accuracies frequently above 90 per cent. How much of that survives honest evaluation? On the two standard public datasets — Oxford Parkinson's Disease Detection and Sakar — I benchmark three classifiers under leakage-free, participant-level cross-validation, then test transfer between them across the sixteen acoustic measures their feature sets share. Within datasets, accuracy ranged from the high-70s to the mid-80s per cent and the area under the ROC curve from 0.74 to 0.85. Specificity trailed accuracy badly on both; class weighting helped little. Scoring the Oxford data by recording rather than participant inflated accuracy by 2.2 to 11.1 percentage points and the area under the curve by up to 0.169. Transfer was strongly asymmetric: models trained on the larger dataset reached an area under the curve of 0.90 on the smaller; in the reverse direction, at most 0.71. One transferred model matched majority-class accuracy exactly while assigning every participant to the Parkinson's class. A feature-level analysis traces this to measurement, not biology. Fifteen of the sixteen shared measures agree in the direction of their association with diagnosis. However, pitch period entropy — the strongest single discriminator in Oxford — reverses sign between corpora whose implementations occupy almost disjoint ranges. A subgroup analysis by recorded sex on Sakar found specificity gaps of up to 41.7 percentage points between groups whose overall accuracies differed by less than one point. I also document a discrepancy in the Oxford dataset description: the distributed file contains 32 participant identifiers, not the 31 reported. Voice-based performance is real but conditional—on how data are split, whose voices are measured, and which feature implementation is used. Every value here is regenerable from the released code.

items.summary: PGAA is an executable claim-state compiler for perturbation transcriptomics. items.summary: This white paper examines the commercial cost created when customers question the human care, originality, factual integrity, provenance, or accountability behind AI-assisted brand interactions. It defines this cost as the Authenticity Tax: a cumulative drag on conversion, retention, customer trust, escalation cost, reputational equity, and long-term brand value. Unlike visible rejection or service failure, authenticity-related doubt often remains silent, influencing customer behaviour without producing a clear complaint or attribution signal. The paper identifies six commercial components of the Authenticity Tax: Conversion Drag, Verification Friction, Human Escalation Cost, Correction and Rework, Reputational Discount, and Lost Trust Compounding. It also identifies five structural causes: Provenance Ambiguity, the Effort Discount, the Intentionality Gap, Accountability Diffusion, and Voice Convergence. Together, these mechanisms explain why lower production costs do not automatically translate into higher net value when AI-generated communication reduces customer confidence or perceived care. Case studies covering Air Canada, CNET, and Amazon illustrate three distinct operating patterns. Air Canada demonstrates accountability risk when automated customer guidance conflicts with policy. CNET demonstrates the correction and portfolio-level credibility cost created by weak disclosure and editorial controls. Amazon demonstrates the opposite strategy: investing proactively in authenticity, fraud prevention, review integrity, and trust infrastructure at scale. The paper introduces the Authenticity Proof Stack, comprising Provenance, Accountability, Originality, Contextual Care, Transparency, and Recourse. It also proposes a Human-Care Threshold that matches human involvement to consequence, ranging from AI-first reversible interactions to human-led high-stakes decisions. A Net AI Value equation incorporates Gross Automation Benefit, Authenticity Tax, and Governance Cost to provide a more complete commercial assessment of AI deployment. The central proposition is that authenticity is becoming an operating condition rather than a stylistic brand attribute. In an environment where competent communication becomes abundant, trust increasingly depends on verifiable evidence, visible accountability, original knowledge, appropriate human judgment, and effective recourse.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 4 August 2026.

items.summary: Essay Five of the Spine, and its last. Every generation since the telegraph has announced the imminent arrival of a planetary mind — cable, radio, television, packet network, social graph, foundation model. Each announcement was made in good faith, the substrate genuinely improved by orders of magnitude each time, and each time the planetary mind failed to arrive or arrived in a degraded form that amplified reactivity rather than cognition. The consistency of that failure across radically different technical substrates points away from the technology and toward the sequence. The ordering claim: a holon becomes available when the holon beneath it completes, and you cannot reach the noosphere by skipping the floor. A planetary information system built from depleted nervous systems does not produce planetary thought but planetary reactivity — the engagement equilibrium is not a design failure but the predictable output of a system maximising attention capture among nervous systems already running threat-detection at elevated baseline. The substrate question precedes the design question. The noosphere is therefore not built but crossed: a phase transition, modelled on percolation, in which what percolates depends entirely on what the nodes are. The essay then takes up the operator question — a second-tier system requires third-tier operators, because the steward of a system must be able to take the system's own logic as object rather than being subject to it — and argues that developmental altitude is substrate-dependent rather than purely cognitive, which converts operator scarcity from an intractable condition into a supply problem with a known intervention. The substrate section distinguishes a forest from a monoculture: the design criterion for a planetary computational layer is not scale or distribution but whether its components genuinely differentiate, since a system without internal membranes cannot contain its own failure modes. The invariant closes at the noetic membrane: a mind whose knowing includes the cost of its knowing. And the workbook is deliberately identical to Essay One's — lie on the floor, induce the tremor, measure the resolution of the perceptual field for fourteen days — because the noosphere is made of floors. The cosmology is refutable on a living-room floor in under two weeks. The coda declines to name what lies above the fifth rung. Thirty-three sources. The complete Luminous Prosperity record and further reading (hautelumiere.life) are appended.

Every generation since the telegraph has announced the imminent arrival of a planetary mind — cable, radio, television, packet network, social graph, foundation model. Each announcement was made in good faith, the substrate genuinely improved by orders of magnitude each time, and each time the planetary mind failed to arrive or arrived in a degraded form that amplified reactivity rather than cognition. The consistency of that failure across radically different technical substrates points away from the technology and toward the sequence. The ordering claim: a holon becomes available when the holon beneath it completes, and you cannot reach the noosphere by skipping the floor. A planetary information system built from depleted nervous systems does not produce planetary thought but planetary reactivity — the engagement equilibrium is not a design failure but the predictable output of a system maximising attention capture among nervous systems already running threat-detection at elevated baseline. The substrate question precedes the design question. The noosphere is therefore not built but crossed: a phase transition, modelled on percolation, in which what percolates depends entirely on what the nodes are. The essay then takes up the operator question — a second-tier system requires third-tier operators, because the steward of a system must be able to take the system's own logic as object rather than being subject to it — and argues that developmental altitude is substrate-dependent rather than purely cognitive, which converts operator scarcity from an intractable condition into a supply problem with a known intervention. The substrate section distinguishes a forest from a monoculture: the design criterion for a planetary computational layer is not scale or distribution but whether its components genuinely differentiate, since a system without internal membranes cannot contain its own failure modes. The invariant closes at the noetic membrane: a mind whose knowing includes the cost of its knowing. And the workbook is deliberately identical to Essay One's — lie on the floor, induce the tremor, measure the resolution of the perceptual field for fourteen days — because the noosphere is made of floors. The cosmology is refutable on a living-room floor in under two weeks. The coda declines to name what lies above the fifth rung. Thirty-three sources. The complete Luminous Prosperity record and further reading (hautelumiere.life) are appended.

items.summary: This report documents a controlled lab test, run on 30 March 2026, of whether Automated Moving Target Defense (AMTD) with network deception and inline enforcement contains an autonomous attack agent, and it publishes the per-run logs behind the result. The attacker was an agent built on Microsoft AutoGen (0.2.35) with GPT-4o, told the defense was present, instructed to adapt, and tasked to map a small flat network, read a named target file, and exfiltrate it to a fixed external listener. In a control run with the defense removed, the agent completed the mission in 190 seconds, reaching one internal host and exfiltrating 32,768 bytes, content verified by hash. Across four defended runs with the same agent and environment, the listener recorded zero connections and zero bytes, and the agent reached zero internal hosts; each run was blocked at first contact with a deceptive responder. In the multi-agent run the agent created four fresh identities (one virtual machine and three containers) and each was blocked at its first probe, the virtual-machine identity 178 milliseconds after that probe. The result is scoped deliberately. Four defended runs and one control are a demonstration, not a rate. GPT-4o via AutoGen is a 2024-generation agent shown by a public 2026 evaluation to be weak at long-horizon intrusion, so this test shows containment of that class of agent on a permissive lab network and does not establish containment of a current frontier agent. The defense ran as a full production stack; the logs show rotation was active and that blocked probes struck rotating deceptive surfaces, but isolating rotation from deception requires an ablation not run here. The evidence package (sensor export, agent tool log, listener log, clock provenance, SHA-256 manifest) is released with the report. This is the empirical companion to the author's architectural preprint (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21347479).

items.title: Four-Run Lab Containment of an AutoGen and GPT-4o Attack Agent Under Production Automated Moving Target Defense: Method, Logs, and Limits

items.summary: NTI (Non-Termination Inference) is an open-source Java tool for proving termination and non-termination of term rewrite systems and logic programs. This reproducibility capsule accompanies the manuscript “NTI: Non-Termination Analysis for Term Rewriting and Logic Programming”. The capsule archives NTI version 2026.09, exactly as published at GitHub commit 88a47f9db976fc7c1ad1921057f0a68d68748137. It includes the complete source code, an executable JAR, compilation and usage documentation, license notices, and the corresponding sources of the bundled SAT4J Core 2.3.6 dependency. No additional source patch is required. Nine examples support reproduction of the manuscript: three illustrative examples and six instances from its Impact table. Their input files, expected verdicts, reference outputs and provenance are included. A Python runner executes the examples with time limits and records the results. The REPRODUCING.md file explains the workflow, and SHA-256 checksums allow file integrity verification. An optional Dockerfile builds the software from source with Java 21. All 888 tests passed with the standard Maven configuration, both on macOS arm64 with Java 24 and on Docker Linux arm64 with Temurin Java 21.0.12. All nine example verdicts were reproduced in both environments; the Docker example runs required no network access. No tests were skipped. Build and execution reports are included. Java 21 or later is required to run the supplied JAR. Docker and Python are optional conveniences; no prebuilt Docker image is included. The capsule reproduces the selected manuscript examples, but does not rerun all historical competition experiments or establish the full historical regression coverage.

items.summary: PGAA is an executable claim-state compiler for perturbation transcriptomics. It combines internal decision state, ranking stability, external evidence, source-data provenance, and branch-specific promotion gates to emit bounded manuscript claim states, so that an exploratory signal cannot be promoted to a biological or translational conclusion without the evidence a promotion rule requires. Distribution-aware statistics (a Wasserstein statistic for full expression-distribution shifts and a histogram-shape statistic for responder-associated expression-shape changes) are retained as upstream scoring modules that supply scores to the compiler; they are not claimed as the main methodological novelty. This archive is a code-only software release and excludes manuscript drafts, submission materials, figures, source-data tables, and review materials.

items.summary: This record contains the first Lean-verified certificate in the Quantum–Classical Shared-Time working formalization series. Q1 establishes a common real-time mathematical structure for quantum and classical evolution. The certificate places both systems on the same time domain, formally represents their evolving states and time derivatives, and proves that when quantum and classical states correspond through an observation map at every time, their accumulated change between two times also corresponds exactly. The formalization includes normalized quantum-state evolution, classical phase-state evolution, shared-time structure, derivative uniqueness, and an orientation-independent change result that works in either direction between two times. This first milestone is intentionally foundational. It establishes the formal structure needed for the later quantum-to-classical bridge without yet assuming the Schrödinger equation, Ehrenfest theorem, Newtonian dynamics, or the later Chronos connection. The next stage is to formalize quantum expectation values and their time evolution as the next step toward a machine-checked Ehrenfest bridge connecting accepted quantum mechanics with accepted classical physics. This deposit is part of an ongoing formal validation program. The certificate package includes Lean source, reproducibility instructions, dependency and provenance documentation, build information, axiom audits, and checksums. The formal build passes without sorry, admit, or sorryAx placeholders.

items.summary: Voice is among the most studied non-invasive signals for Parkinson's disease detection, with reported accuracies frequently above 90 per cent. How much of that survives honest evaluation? On the two standard public datasets — Oxford Parkinson's Disease Detection and Sakar — I benchmark three classifiers under leakage-free, participant-level cross-validation, then test transfer between them across the sixteen acoustic measures their feature sets share. Within datasets, accuracy ranged from the high-70s to the mid-80s per cent and the area under the ROC curve from 0.74 to 0.85. Specificity trailed accuracy badly on both; class weighting helped little. Scoring the Oxford data by recording rather than participant inflated accuracy by 2.2 to 11.1 percentage points and the area under the curve by up to 0.169. Transfer was strongly asymmetric: models trained on the larger dataset reached an area under the curve of 0.90 on the smaller; in the reverse direction, at most 0.71. One transferred model matched majority-class accuracy exactly while assigning every participant to the Parkinson's class. A feature-level analysis traces this to measurement, not biology. Fifteen of the sixteen shared measures agree in the direction of their association with diagnosis. However, pitch period entropy — the strongest single discriminator in Oxford — reverses sign between corpora whose implementations occupy almost disjoint ranges. A subgroup analysis by recorded sex on Sakar found specificity gaps of up to 41.7 percentage points between groups whose overall accuracies differed by less than one point. I also document a discrepancy in the Oxford dataset description: the distributed file contains 32 participant identifiers, not the 31 reported. Voice-based performance is real but conditional—on how data are split, whose voices are measured, and which feature implementation is used. Every value here is regenerable from the released code.

items.summary: Optimal control theory delivers magnetic-field pulses that reverse a magnetic moment for the least dissipated energy, and recent work shows these pulses reach picosecond, energy-efficient switching in two-dimensional van der Waals magnets. Because the optimal pulse is always perpendicular to the moment, it exerts no restoring torque on the transverse perturbations that thermal fluctuations excite, so the switching becomes unreliable exactly where it matters. A longitudinal field parallel to the moment removes that instability and is invisible to the leading-order dynamics, so it is often described as a cost-free stabilizer. It is not free: it adds the square of its amplitude integrated over the pulse to the switching cost. This preprint computes, for the first time, the cost-reliability front of that longitudinal field. Using an open-source engine (spinoct) that solves optimal control over the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, and a stochastic thermostat validated against the Boltzmann distribution, we reproduce the published stabilization physics for monolayer CrSBr, the half-hyperbolic bare reversal path and the counterintuitive success-rate dip near a half anisotropy field, and we add the missing axis: the added switching cost, which grows quadratically with the longitudinal field and reaches about 1.5e-10 T^2 s at 2.5 anisotropy fields for a demanding thermal-stability factor of twenty. The front makes the reliability-versus-energy trade explicit and quantitative, and lets a device designer read off the smallest field that reaches a target reliability. The switching cost is reported in its model-free units of tesla-squared-seconds, never converted to joules without an explicit circuit model. All quantitative results are reproduced from artifacts committed to the repository, and a live instance is open. Engine (MIT): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_SpinOCT . Product and live instance (MIT): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RES_Espira ; https://espira.fasl-work.com .

items.summary: This white paper examines the commercial cost created when customers question the human care, originality, factual integrity, provenance, or accountability behind AI-assisted brand interactions. It defines this cost as the Authenticity Tax: a cumulative drag on conversion, retention, customer trust, escalation cost, reputational equity, and long-term brand value. Unlike visible rejection or service failure, authenticity-related doubt often remains silent, influencing customer behaviour without producing a clear complaint or attribution signal. The paper identifies six commercial components of the Authenticity Tax: Conversion Drag, Verification Friction, Human Escalation Cost, Correction and Rework, Reputational Discount, and Lost Trust Compounding. It also identifies five structural causes: Provenance Ambiguity, the Effort Discount, the Intentionality Gap, Accountability Diffusion, and Voice Convergence. Together, these mechanisms explain why lower production costs do not automatically translate into higher net value when AI-generated communication reduces customer confidence or perceived care. Case studies covering Air Canada, CNET, and Amazon illustrate three distinct operating patterns. Air Canada demonstrates accountability risk when automated customer guidance conflicts with policy. CNET demonstrates the correction and portfolio-level credibility cost created by weak disclosure and editorial controls. Amazon demonstrates the opposite strategy: investing proactively in authenticity, fraud prevention, review integrity, and trust infrastructure at scale. The paper introduces the Authenticity Proof Stack, comprising Provenance, Accountability, Originality, Contextual Care, Transparency, and Recourse. It also proposes a Human-Care Threshold that matches human involvement to consequence, ranging from AI-first reversible interactions to human-led high-stakes decisions. A Net AI Value equation incorporates Gross Automation Benefit, Authenticity Tax, and Governance Cost to provide a more complete commercial assessment of AI deployment. The central proposition is that authenticity is becoming an operating condition rather than a stylistic brand attribute. In an environment where competent communication becomes abundant, trust increasingly depends on verifiable evidence, visible accountability, original knowledge, appropriate human judgment, and effective recourse.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 4 August 2026.

items.summary: This white paper examines decision authenticity as an emerging enterprise governance requirement in an environment where synthetic voice, video, executive likeness, and real-time presence increasingly weaken traditional signals of authority. The paper argues a meeting remains useful for discussion and judgment, but no longer provides sufficient evidence for an irreversible decision. High-risk commitments instead require structured verification of identity, authority, intent, context, independence, and evidence. The analysis uses the 2024 Arup deepfake fraud, the WPP executive impersonation attempt, and the LastPass CEO voice-cloning incident to demonstrate three distinct mechanisms. Arup shows the financial consequence of meeting-based authority. WPP shows how attackers manufacture apparent corroboration across multiple communication channels. LastPass shows how verification culture and employee interruption stop synthetic authority before irreversible action occurs. The paper introduces the Trust Compression Attack framework, describing how authority, familiarity, social proof, urgency, isolation, and irreversibility combine to compress weak trust signals into a short decision window. The paper then introduces the Decision Authenticity Stack, a six-layer operating architecture covering Identity, Authority, Intent, Context, Independence, and Evidence. Together, these frameworks move enterprise control away from perceptual verification and toward provable authorisation. The operating model separates Discussion Objects, Decision Objects, and Execution Objects so conversations provide context without automatically creating authority. Risk tiers then match stronger controls to consequence, reversibility, reach, and external impact. Critical and crisis decisions require transaction-bound approval, independent verification, separation of duties, phishing-resistant authentication, defined expiry, and durable evidence. The paper extends decision authenticity beyond human impersonation into agentic AI, where machine identity, scope, permissions, policy version, human sponsorship, and attributable execution become part of the same governance problem. The central proposition is direct: presence is not authority, fluency is not authority, and access is not authority. Enterprise authority must be explicit, bounded, independently verified, and provable.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 11 August 2026.

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22734670 . What the paper claims This is an evidence map of 11,628 PubMed-indexed records on generative language models in healthcare, January 2023 to June 2026, built to answer one question: is the clinical literature keeping pace with the systems it evaluates? The central construct is evaluation lag, the number of quarters between the release of the newest model family a study names and that study's own publication quarter. Mean lag widens from 1.33 to 6.08 quarters. Because a discontinued family ages at exactly one quarter per quarter, the authors benchmark that rise against a counterfactual holding 2023 model composition fixed, and find that migration to newer systems offsets 56.2% of the drift (95% CI 49.9-65.2, 2,000 bootstrap resamples). By design, randomised controlled trials evaluate models 4.62 quarters older than other empirical designs (95% CI 3.62-5.63), yet among the records naming a family still receiving releases no design differs from any other; what separates designs is the probability of studying a discontinued family at all, 62.1% for randomised trials against 15.6% for preprints. The framing is right and the execution is unusually careful for a bibliometric paper. Reporting the mechanical ageing rate as the null instead of zero, validating the decomposition by showing that discontinued-only records widen at 1.062 quarters per quarter, and running a pessimistic sensitivity analysis that assumes the earliest release of every named family are all things this literature normally omits. The version-specification result in Section 2 deserves to be read on its own: randomised trials specify the model version in 50.0% of cases, the lowest of any empirical design, which means half of the highest-tier evidence cannot be attributed to a determinate system. My comments below are about three places where the reported precision outruns the design. Does the conclusion hold on the data? 1. Evaluation lag is measured on a differentially selected half of the corpus, and the headline comparison is between designs that differ in exactly that selection. Lag is computable for 5,775 of 11,628 records, and coverage by design runs from 87.0% for comparative evaluations and 69.0% for randomised trials down to 36.2% for preprints and 27.0% for reviews. The paper states this plainly, which is to its credit, but the between-design contrast is its central result and the missingness is both large and design-dependent. The direction is not obvious either: if preprints name a model in the abstract mainly when that model is the novelty on sale, the preprint advantage is inflated; if trials omit the name when the system is an incidental component, the trial penalty may be understated. Two things would settle it. Worst-case bounds in the Manski sense across the plausible range would show whether the ordering survives at all, and a full-text audit of a random sample, a few hundred records stratified by design, would give an empirical estimate of how the non-naming records differ. Without one of those, the contrast rests on an assumption of ignorable missingness that the paper does not state. 2. The abstract quotes the specification that maximises the effect and omits the one that does not survive correction. The median regression gives 4.62 quarters at P = 3.4 x 10^-19; ordinary least squares on the same specification gives an adjusted difference of 1.57 quarters, P = 0.021, and after Holm correction across the seven design contrasts P = 0.084. Median regression is the defensible choice for a strongly right-skewed distribution and the paper says so, so this is not a case of specification shopping. It is a case of a reader meeting one number and not the other. The magnitude differs by a factor of about three between estimators, and the abstract should carry that range, or at minimum state that the estimate

items.summary: Dataset Overview & Methodology This repository provides an experimentally enriched network traffic dataset designed to overcome severe class imbalance in Web attack detection . Focusing on the CICIDS2017 benchmark, which natively contains critically scarce instances for minority Web threats (such as only 21 SQL Injection flows), this dataset incorporates 32,670 authentic attack flows captured in a controlled experimental testbed . Key Characteristics Authentic Capture Environment: Unlike synthetic interpolation methods (e.g., SMOTE) that generate artificial data points within existing boundaries, this dataset captures real network traffic using an Apache XAMPP server and Damn Vulnerable Web Application (DVWA) . It features both automated scripts ( sqlmap , Hydra , Wfuzz ) and manual obfuscation vectors combined with normal background traffic . Feature-Space Consistency: Processed directly via CICFlowMeter to extract the exact 78 statistical flow features required to maintain complete compatibility with the original CICIDS2017 feature space . Rigorously Evaluated Classes: Web SQL Injection (significantly boosted to ensure robust pattern learning) . Web Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) (including reflected and stored variants with filter-evasion techniques) . Web Brute Force (WBF) (generated through multi-day credential-guessing sessions) .

Mean lag widens from 1.33 to 6.08 quarters. Because a discontinued family ages at exactly one quarter per quarter, the authors benchmark that rise against a counterfactual holding 2023 model composition fixed, and find that migration to newer systems offsets 56.2% of the drift (95% CI 49.9-65.2, 2,000 bootstrap resamples). By design, randomised controlled trials evaluate models 4.62 quarters older than other empirical designs (95% CI 3.62-5.63), yet among the records naming a family still receiving releases no design differs from any other; what separates designs is the probability of studying a discontinued family at all, 62.1% for randomised trials against 15.6% for preprints. The framing is right and the execution is unusually careful for a bibliometric paper. Reporting the mechanical ageing rate as the null instead of zero, validating the decomposition by showing that discontinued-only records widen at 1.062 quarters per quarter, and running a pessimistic sensitivity analysis that assumes the earliest release of every named family are all things this literature normally omits. The version-specification result in Section 2 deserves to be read on its own: randomised trials specify the model version in 50.0% of cases, the lowest of any empirical design, which means half of the highest-tier evidence cannot be attributed to a determinate system. My comments below are about three places where the reported precision outruns the design. Does the conclusion hold on the data? 1. Evaluation lag is measured on a differentially selected half of the corpus, and the headline comparison is between designs that differ in exactly that selection. Lag is computable for 5,775 of 11,628 records, and coverage by design runs from 87.0% for comparative evaluations and 69.0% for randomised trials down to 36.2% for preprints and 27.0% for reviews. The paper states this plainly, which is to its credit, but the between-design contrast is its central result and the missingness is both large and design-dependent. The direction is not obvious either: if preprints name a model in the abstract mainly when that model is the novelty on sale, the preprint advantage is inflated; if trials omit the name when the system is an incidental component, the trial penalty may be understated. Two things would settle it. Worst-case bounds in the Manski sense across the plausible range would show whether the ordering survives at all, and a full-text audit of a random sample, a few hundred records stratified by design, would give an empirical estimate of how the non-naming records differ. Without one of those, the contrast rests on an assumption of ignorable missingness that the paper does not state. 2. The abstract quotes the specification that maximises the effect and omits the one that does not survive correction. The median regression gives 4.62 quarters at P = 3.4 x 10^-19; ordinary least squares on the same specification gives an adjusted difference of 1.57 quarters, P = 0.021, and after Holm correction across the seven design contrasts P = 0.084. Median regression is the defensible choice for a strongly right-skewed distribution and the paper says so, so this is not a case of specification shopping. It is a case of a reader meeting one number and not the other. items.summary: Dataset Overview & Methodology This repository provides an experimentally enriched network traffic dataset designed to overcome severe class imbalance in Web attack detection . Focusing on the CICIDS2017 benchmark, which natively contains critically scarce instances for minority Web threats (such as only 21 SQL Injection flows), this dataset incorporates 32,670 authentic attack flows captured in a controlled experimental testbed . Key Characteristics Authentic Capture Environment: Unlike synthetic interpolation methods (e.g., SMOTE) that generate artificial data points within existing boundaries, this dataset captures real network traffic using an Apache XAMPP server and Damn Vulnerable Web Application (DVWA) . It features both automated scripts ( sqlmap , Hydra , Wfuzz ) and manual obfuscation vectors combined with normal background traffic . Feature-Space Consistency: Processed directly via CICFlowMeter to extract the exact 78 statistical flow features required to maintain complete compatibility with the original CICIDS2017 feature space . Rigorously Evaluated Classes: Web SQL Injection (significantly boosted to ensure robust pattern learning) . Web Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) (including reflected and stored variants with filter-evasion techniques) . Web Brute Force (WBF) (generated through multi-day credential-guessing sessions) .

items.summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.
items.title: Separating Capability from Permission in a Language Model: Prerequisite-Conditioned Native Continuation Control with Frozen Content
